sources.entry: cx-Freeze - Converts Python scripts into standalone executables and installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

summary.one_liner: cx_Freeze is a cross-platform tool that turns Python scripts into standalone executables.
summary.what_it_does: The README says cx_Freeze creates standalone executables from Python scripts, aiming for the same performance as the original script. It is described as cross-platform, working on any platform that Python runs on. Installation is covered via pip (into a virtual environment) and conda-forge. The README also mentions a development build install path and a separate guide for creating "service" executables. Documentation, a changelog, and a discussion channel are linked, but the README itself gives no detail on the freezing process or options. The awesome-python listing describes it as producing installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux, which the README itself does not spell out.
use_cases: package a Python script as a standalone executable
distribute a Python app to users without Python installed
build Windows, macOS, or Linux executables from Python
freeze a Python service into an executable
notable: Cross-platform: works on any platform Python runs on, per the README
Separate documentation covers creating service executables
Development builds can be installed with pip --pre
caveats: README is brief and defers most details to external documentation
Development build install requires uninstalling the released version first
summary.license: Derived from the Python Software Foundation License (per README)
